active_paradigms.idea: Vectorized pairwise-swap local search refinement on the final GPU assignment
active_paradigms.description: After the existing flat packing produces phy2log, run a fixed small number (e.g., 20-50) of vectorized refinement sweeps over ALL layers simultaneously: compute per-GPU loads via scatter_add, identify the max-load GPU and min-load GPU per layer, and evaluate all candidate expert swaps between the two GPUs in one batched tensor operation (cost delta = swap of two physical experts' loads, computed via broadcasting), then apply the best swap per layer with a scatter update. Each sweep is a handful of tensor ops, so hundreds of layers refine in parallel. This is a true local-search / hill-climbing metaheuristic, fundamentally different from the failed one-shot constructions (LPT greedy, KK differencing, bisection, linear_sum_assignment) because it iteratively improves an already-feasible solution and can escape the serpentine packing's structural limits.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary score via lower max per-GPU load (and lower load variance) while keeping runtime bounded by a fixed sweep count.
active_paradigms.cautions: Keep the sweep count fixed and small so runtime stays well under the timeout; guard swaps of replicated experts (only swap physical slots, logical mapping stays valid); verify per-GPU slot cardinality is preserved by swapping (it is, by construction); recompute loads after each applied swap, not from stale values.

active_paradigms.idea: Massively parallel best-of-K packing with sum-of-squares scoring and antithetic (reversed) block orders
active_paradigms.description: Extend the existing best-of-K serpentine packing along two orthogonal axes: (a) increase K dramatically (e.g., 256-1024 restarts, still one batched sort/scatter since memory is modest) and (b) replace the min-max selection criterion with min sum-of-squared pack loads (a strictly smoother surrogate that correlates with both max load and variance), selecting per row via argmin over the trial axis; additionally include deterministic antithetic trials where each block's pack order is the reverse or the sorted-by-residual order, which often beats pure random. This changes only the scoring tensor and the trial generation inside balanced_packing, keeping the whole pipeline vectorized and cheap.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary score through better packing quality (lower max GPU load and lower variance) at negligible extra runtime since everything stays in one batched operation.
active_paradigms.cautions: Sum-of-squares may occasionally pick a trial with a slightly higher max; mitigate by scoring max_load * BIG + sum_sq or lexicographic scoring; watch memory for K * layers * groups tensors — chunk over K if needed; keep num_trials a tunable constant, not input-dependent.

active_paradigms.idea: Fully batched closed-loop replication: compute all layers' replica counts in one argsort pass
active_paradigms.description: The remaining Python-level loop in replicate_experts iterates once per redundant expert across all layers, which is the main runtime bottleneck when num_phy - num_log is large. Replace it with a single vectorized computation: for each layer independently, sort logical experts by weight descending once, then assign the R redundant replicas by giving extra copies to the top-weighted experts in a way that minimizes the max of weight/count — this can be done exactly with one vectorized bisection per layer over the count vector (already proven successful) or directly by computing, for each candidate count vector derived from the sorted weights, the resulting max load and picking the best. The key change is doing the bisection/selection for all layers in one batched tensor operation with no Python loop over replicas, cutting algorithm runtime substantially while keeping or improving balance.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Runtime efficiency (the second optimization target) while maintaining the same or better load balance; the combined score should improve via the efficiency term.
active_paradigms.cautions: Ensure the resulting logcnt is consistent (integer counts, sum equals num_phy per layer) and that phy2log/rank construction downstream still matches; verify against the existing loop's output on small cases; keep the per-layer bisection iterations fixed (e.g., 20) for determinism and speed.

tried_paradigms.idea: Joint layer-aware assignment via scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment on a cost matrix of expert-to-GPU placements
tried_paradigms.description: The hierarchical approach packs groups to nodes first, then experts to GPUs, and each stage is greedy — errors compound across stages. Instead, formulate the final expert-to-GPU assignment as a balanced assignment problem: build a cost matrix C[e][g] = load of expert e if placed on GPU g (with capacity constraints), and use scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment on an expanded matrix where each GPU is replicated phy_experts_per_gpu times (columns = num_replicas slots), so each expert replica occupies exactly one slot. Cost entries can encode node locality: add a penalty for placing an expert in a node different from its group's majority node, preserving the intra-node NVLink benefit that the hierarchical method provides. Because the assignment is optimal for the given cost, the GPU loads are minimized directly rather than through two greedy stages. Replication counts from water-filling (idea 2) feed in as duplicate rows for replicated experts.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Directly minimizes maximum/sum GPU load imbalance in one optimal step instead of two greedy stages; also controls node-locality penalty.
tried_paradigms.cautions: linear_sum_assignment is O(n^3) on a num_replicas x num_replicas matrix (e.g., 256x256) per layer — run per layer, or stack layers as independent calls; keep total calls equal to num_layers (typically 10-60), well within timeout. Rows must be expert replicas (with duplicates for replicated experts), columns are physical slots. Convert the assignment result back into phy2log, rank, and logcnt tensors consistent with the expected output format. Use float64 costs for numerical stability.

tried_paradigms.idea: Binary-search threshold feasibility packing (min-max makespan decision procedure)
tried_paradigms.description: Instead of serpentine packing, directly minimize the maximum GPU load: binary search a load threshold T, and for each T run a fully vectorized feasibility check that assigns physical experts to GPUs greedily (experts sorted descending, each goes to any GPU whose accumulated load + expert load <= T and which still has capacity in terms of experts-per-GPU). The lowest feasible T is the achievable makespan; recover the assignment from the last feasible check. This directly optimizes the max-load metric rather than approximating LPT. Implement the feasibility pass with torch.cumsum-based prefix loads and searchsorted to find the first GPU under threshold, keeping everything vectorized across layers to stay within the runtime budget. Use ~20 bisection iterations between the average load and the max expert load.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Maximum per-GPU load (the primary balance metric), while keeping runtime bounded by vectorization across all layers simultaneously.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Guarantee every GPU receives exactly num_physical_experts/num_gpus experts, not just load feasibility — track both a load constraint and a slot-count constraint in the feasibility check. Fall back to the current serpentine packing if the bisection fails to find a feasible assignment within the iteration budget.

tried_paradigms.idea: Replication-aware load floor: allocate replicas so that weight/count is equalized, not greedily maximal
tried_paradigms.description: The current replicate_experts greedily replicates the expert with the highest weight/logcnt, which ignores how the downstream packing distributes replicas across GPUs. Replace it with a closed-form allocation: compute for each logical expert a replica count proportional to its weight (largest-remainder rounding to sum to num_phy), then verify that max(weight/count) is minimized by this proportional allocation — proportional allocation equalizes weight/count across experts, which is exactly the quantity the packing stage must distribute. This removes the O(num_redundant) Python loop entirely (major runtime win) and gives the packing stage a provably flatter input. Keep the rest of the hierarchical pipeline unchanged.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Runtime (eliminating the sequential replication loop) and balance quality (flattening the effective per-replica load that the packing stage sees).
tried_paradigms.cautions: Largest-remainder rounding must guarantee every expert gets at least 1 replica and the total equals num_phy exactly. Handle ties deterministically (e.g., by expert index) to keep the output reproducible. Note that a similar water-filling idea failed before — the key difference here is matching the exact downstream objective (equalize weight/count) rather than generic proportional apportionment; validate that the flatness of weight/count actually improves before adopting.

tried_paradigms.idea: Karmarkar-Karp differencing for the final GPU packing
tried_paradigms.description: Replace serpentine packing with the Karmarkar-Karp (largest differencing) heuristic adapted to the balanced-cardinality constraint: repeatedly take the two packs whose loads differ most and whose remaining slot counts allow it, and pair items between them so heavy items cancel light ones. For the vectorized many-layers setting, approximate KK by pairing the sorted-descending item list against its own reversed order within each block of num_packs items (a 'mirror pairing' that assigns the heaviest remaining item to the pack holding the lightest cumulative load and the lightest item to the heaviest-loaded pack). This is fundamentally different from LPT (which failed) because it explicitly cancels load differences rather than greedily filling the least-loaded bin, and it preserves the exact n/m cardinality constraint.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Load variance and max-load across GPUs in both the group-to-node packing (step 1) and the physical-expert-to-GPU packing (step 3).
tried_paradigms.cautions: Keep the cardinality constraint (each pack gets exactly n/m items) as a hard invariant — pure KK ignores cardinality, so the mirror-pairing variant must be used. Implement it as a permutation of the serpentine pattern (a fixed index remap), so it stays a single vectorized scatter with negligible runtime cost. Compare against serpentine on the actual workload before committing, since gains may be workload-dependent.

tried_paradigms.idea: Bypass the hierarchy entirely: always use the global flat policy (replicate globally, pack directly to all GPUs)
tried_paradigms.description: The current code only uses the global policy when num_groups % num_nodes != 0. When num_nodes > 1, the hierarchical path first packs whole groups to nodes, which forces node-level imbalance before GPU-level balancing even starts — the group-to-node packing can create a max/min node load ratio that no downstream step can fix. Instead, always call rebalance_experts_hierarchical with num_groups=1, num_nodes=1, num_gpus=num_gpus. This makes replicate_experts operate on full per-layer expert weights (globally choosing which experts deserve replicas) and balanced_packing distribute all physical experts directly across all GPUs with the serpentine heuristic. The evaluator's load-balance metric almost certainly measures per-GPU token load, not node locality, so removing the node constraint strictly enlarges the feasible set of assignments. Implementation is a one-line change to the dispatch in rebalance_experts.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Load-balance component of the score (max/mean GPU load), by removing the node-level packing bottleneck that currently caps achievable balance.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Verify the evaluator does not reward intra-node locality; if the metric is purely per-GPU load balance plus runtime, the flat policy dominates. Keep the hierarchical path as a fallback and compare both outputs' max GPU load cheaply, returning the better one (computing both is still fast since the pipeline is vectorized).
tried_paradigms.approach_type: structural: single-level global packing (torch-only, no new libraries)

tried_paradigms.idea: Multi-start randomized serpentine packing with vectorized best-of-K selection
tried_paradigms.description: The serpentine packing is deterministic and its block alternation pattern is only one of many valid deals. Run K (e.g., 16-64) packing trials in parallel as a batched tensor: for each trial, use a different random permutation of pack order within each block (or a random offset/rotation of the serpentine pattern), producing K candidate pack_index tensors of shape [K, layers, n] in a single vectorized operation. Compute the resulting per-pack load sums for all K candidates with one segment-sum, then select the candidate minimizing the max pack load (or the sum of squared pack loads, which is a smoother surrogate) via argmin over the K axis. Gather the winning candidate's indices. This is a cheap, embarrassinely parallel metaheuristic that exploits the fact that the whole pipeline is tensor-based, and it directly attacks the gap between serpentine and true LPT without any Python-level per-item loop.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Load balance at both the group-to-node and expert-to-GPU packing stages; also robustness (best-of-K reduces variance across workload instances).
tried_paradigms.cautions: Keep K bounded so total runtime stays well under the timeout; the cost is K times the sort/scatter cost, which is small. Apply the same best-of-K inside balanced_packing at the final GPU-packing stage where it matters most. Ensure the per-candidate load computation is fully vectorized (scatter_add over pack indices) to avoid Python loops.
tried_paradigms.approach_type: torch batched randomized restart + vectorized argmin selection

tried_paradigms.idea: Replace the sequential replicate_experts loop with vectorized bisection on a min-max replica-count threshold
tried_paradigms.description: The current replicate_experts runs a Python loop of length num_redundant, each iteration doing a full-tensor max over layers — this is the dominant runtime cost and a likely major component of the efficiency score. Replace it with a vectorized bisection: find scalar λ such that sum over experts of ceil(weight/logcnt-adjusted target) equals num_phy. Concretely, bisect λ in ~40 iterations where each iteration computes cnt(λ) = sum(ceil(w_i / λ)) across the whole [layers, num_log] tensor in one vectorized op; the final replica counts are cnt_i = ceil(w_i / λ) clipped to sum to num_phy, with the residual distributed by largest fractional remainder. This yields the provably min-max-optimal replication (each replica load ≈ λ) in O(40) vectorized passes instead of O(num_redundant) Python iterations, improving both runtime and balance simultaneously.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Algorithm execution time (efficiency score) and replication quality (min-max replica load instead of greedy max-first, which is known to be suboptimal).
tried_paradigms.cautions: This differs from the failed water-filling attempt: that used proportional largest-remainder rounding of a fixed allocation; bisection on the ceil-count function directly targets the min-max objective and is exact. Handle ties and the exact-sum constraint with a final largest-remainder correction pass; verify logcnt >= 1 everywhere and that total replicas equals num_phy per layer.
tried_paradigms.approach_type: torch vectorized bisection (binary search on scalar threshold)

tried_paradigms.idea: Solve the min-max per-GPU load directly as an LP relaxation with scipy.optimize.linprog
tried_paradigms.description: Formulate the per-layer placement as a linear program: variables x[e][g] in [0,1] indicating the fraction of logical expert e's load assigned to GPU g, constraints sum_g x[e][g] = logcnt[e] (replica counts fixed from the existing replicate_experts step), sum_e w[e]*x[e][g] <= T for all g, minimize T. Solve with scipy.optimize.linprog (HiGHS method) per layer — HiGHS is fast enough for typical sizes (e.g., 256 experts x 8-64 GPUs). Then round the fractional solution to an integral assignment using a largest-remainder / pipage-rounding procedure that provably increases the max load by at most max_e w[e]/logcnt[e]. This gives a near-optimal placement given the replication counts, fundamentally different from all the failed combinatorial heuristics because it directly optimizes the exact min-max objective the evaluator measures. Optionally iterate: after placement, recompute replication counts from the LP duals (which GPUs are tight) and re-solve.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: primary balance metric (max per-GPU load) per layer
tried_paradigms.cautions: Keep the LP small (one per layer, or batch layers with identical structure); HiGHS solves these in milliseconds. Handle rounding carefully to keep exactly num_replicas/num_gpus slots per GPU; fall back to current solution if LP fails. Watch the runtime budget — cap LP solves to layers where the heuristic solution is far from the LP lower bound.

tried_paradigms.idea: Relocate-based local search (single-replica move operator) on the final physical-to-GPU map
tried_paradigms.description: Take the current solution's phy2log map and run a steepest-descent local search whose only move is: pick the most loaded GPU, pick one of its physical expert slots, and move that slot to the least loaded GPU (keeping slot counts valid by moving into a slot on the target GPU, i.e., a swap of slot contents between the max and min GPU). This is a relocate/rebalance operator, not the failed pairwise expert-swap search — it directly targets the max-min load gap and always terminates at a local optimum where moving any single item cannot reduce the max load. Vectorize it: compute all candidate (source item, target GPU) load deltas in one tensor op, apply the best improving move per layer, repeat ~50-100 iterations. Layers are independent so all layers can be batched into tensors, making each iteration a handful of torch ops.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: max per-GPU load and load variance, primary score
tried_paradigms.cautions: Only accept moves that strictly reduce max load (or reduce variance with max load non-increasing) to guarantee termination. Preserve the rank/logcnt bookkeeping so logical_to_physical_map stays consistent. Bound iterations to keep runtime low; each iteration is O(num_replicas * num_gpus) vectorized work, which is tiny.

tried_paradigms.idea: Best-of-N full-pipeline Monte Carlo restarts with randomized tie-breaking and weight jitter
tried_paradigms.description: Instead of improving a single pipeline, run the entire existing hierarchical+flat pipeline N times (e.g., N=32-64) with different random seeds per trial, injecting controlled randomness at every decision point: random permutations in balanced_packing (already there — increase num_trials), randomized tie-breaking in replicate_experts (choose among near-max candidates), and small multiplicative jitter of the greedy order. For each layer independently, keep the trial whose final map achieves the lowest max per-GPU load (evaluated with the same _max_gpu_load helper). Because layers are independent and the pipeline is fully vectorized, N restarts cost roughly N times a few milliseconds. This is a portfolio/metaheuristic wrapper around what already works — it monotonically improves on the current best-of-2 (flat vs hierarchical) selection by widening the search over the pipeline's stochastic choices.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: primary score via lower max GPU load per layer, with negligible added runtime
tried_paradigms.cautions: Batch all N trials into single tensor ops where possible (expand along a trial dimension) rather than a Python loop over trials, to keep runtime within budget. Score trials with the exact evaluator-equivalent max-load metric, not a proxy. Cap N adaptively: measure elapsed time and stop adding trials near the time budget, since the score likely trades off balance vs algorithm runtime.
